rows.name: CCBHC Planning, Development & Implementation (SM-26-014)
rows.program: Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics PDI
rows.heart: 94 CCBHCs are writing applications right now — MORE goes in as their evidence-based line item and strengthens their scoring. Nonprofits and local government only, so this is a pure partner play: the insert kit goes out before the 17th.
rows.eligibility: Statutorily limited: community-based BH nonprofits; local-government behavioral health authorities; IHS/tribal orgs; Urban Indian Organizations. Must be Medicaid-enrolled and serve ≥200 unduplicated clients/yr. For-profits cannot apply.
rows.portal: Grants.gov (partners apply; MORE rides as line item)
rows.accounts_needed: Partner needs SAM/UEI + Grants.gov + eRA Commons (NOFO: register ≥6 weeks before deadline)
rows.page_limit: Project Narrative 15 pp (over = not reviewed); Abstract 1 pp; timeline attachment ≤2 pp
rows.attachments: 16 attachments incl. letters of commitment (#1), licensure + Medicaid proof (#11 — application not reviewed without it), state BH authority approval letter (#16)
rows.scoring_map: Criterion C names the EBP (5 pts, ~1 page — the MORE slot) + Criterion B implementation/staffing (35 pts, mandated workforce training on evidence-based non-pharmacological interventions); +5 priority pts for the 100 highest overdose-death counties (NOFO Appendix C) — that county list is the campaign targeting list
rows.notes: Award up to $1M/yr for up to 4 yrs; expected award 2026-11-15. Companion NOFOs same 8/17 deadline: SM-26-015 (117 existing clinics) and SM-26-016 (12 state planning grants) — tracked as separate rows; ONE insert-kit campaign covers all three. Campaign go/no-go = open decision #5.

rows.name: NIH/NIDA SBIR Phase I (PA-27-100)
rows.program: Parent SBIR (R43/R44) Clinical Trial Optional
rows.heart: The one big pot built for for-profits — R&D money for the MORE app and training platform. Eric wants the ~$2M path; Phase I is the door, first standard due date Sep 5.
rows.eligibility: US for-profit small business, ≤500 employees, majority US-owned — More Therapy qualifies as-is.
rows.accounts_needed: SAM/UEI (annual renewal) + SBA Company Registry + eRA Commons + Grants.gov — 6+ weeks of lead; start now
rows.scoring_map: NIH 5-criteria review — Significance (pain+OUD unmet need), Innovation (~3× CBT effect), Approach, Investigators, Environment; NIDA caps Phase I $400K / Phase II $3M
rows.notes: Dr. Garland owns; Phase I outline this week. Stated due date is Sep 5 (a Saturday; NIH next-business-day rollover lands Tue Sep 8 — plan for Sep 5). Earliest submission 2026-08-05. Later standard dates: 2027-01-05, 2027-04-05; announcement expires 2027-04-06. NIH Guide URL PA-27-100.html 404s — simpler.grants.gov link is the live authoritative text.

rows.name: Texas OAFC — Fall 2026 CORE grants
rows.program: CORE grant cycle
rows.heart: Settlement money with provider-friendly eligibility, opening this fall. Watch page and GovDelivery list are live; position before it posts.
rows.eligibility: For-profits eligible, conditionally: must engage in business in Texas (TX employees or fixed place of business, 34 TAC 16.205) as a condition of award; out-of-state at application time is allowed.
rows.accounts_needed: TX OGMS account; TX SmartBuy/CMBL ($70/yr) for vendor path
rows.notes: Regional program: $75M split across 20 RHP regions by fixed percentages, one application per region, award ceiling 50% of a region's funds (avg region ≈ $3.75M → ceiling ≈ $1.875M). No NOFA posted as of 8/4 ('No grant opportunities are currently open'). Join Comptroller GovDelivery list (L0 pass).

rows.heart: For-profits are explicitly eligible — rare for federal treatment money. FY26 closed Jul 8; no FY27 forecast is posted yet, so the radar watches while we prep the rural partner map to apply day one.
rows.eligibility: For-profits explicitly eligible; rural service area required.
rows.scoring_map: FY26 shape: Planning HRSA-26-036 $100K × 40 ($4M) · Impact HRSA-26-037 $60M ~80 awards at a $750K per-award CEILING (not minimum) · plus a TA NOFO (HRSA-26-038)

rows.name: OneOhio Recovery Foundation — Cycle 3
rows.program: Regional grant cycle 3
rows.heart: For-profits eligible; Cycle 2 was $45.7M. Roughly annual — verify More Therapy's 2-year Ohio registration now so eligibility is ready when it opens.

rows.name: NIH HEAL — Translating Addiction Research into Practice (RFA-DA-27-016)
rows.heart: NIH money a for-profit can hold directly, whose stated priority is exactly MORE's pitch: getting clinicians trained in and delivering evidence-based addiction treatment, with chronic-pain-comorbid SUD named as a priority. An R61 (train clinicians, pilot fidelity) into R33 (implementation trial) built around MORE dissemination.
rows.eligibility: For-profit organizations (incl. small businesses) explicitly eligible.
rows.accounts_needed: SAM/UEI + eRA Commons (SO + PI) + Grants.gov + ORCID — 6+ weeks
rows.page_limit: Standard NIH page limits + 2-pp Timeline and Milestone Plan attachment
rows.scoring_map: Standard NIH peer review; R33 transition is administrative against R61 milestones. NON-RESPONSIVE traps: solely testing new interventions, purely descriptive studies — frame as translation/implementation of the established MORE evidence base.
rows.notes: Posted 2026-06-04; next standard due date 2026-10-09, then 2027-02-10 / 2027-06-09 / … until expiry 2029-02-10; ~12 awards from $6M FY2027. Caps: R61 $350K direct/yr ≤2 yrs (accessible = 2-yr R61 phase); R33 $750K direct/yr ≤5 yrs.

rows.program: IMPOWR Health Systems, RM1 team award

rows.notes: FORECAST ONLY — est. due 2026-11-02, est. start 2027-04-01; the estimated NOFO posting date (2026-04-20) has already slipped (NIH Guide RFA-DA-27-001 404s) so dates may move. No dollar amounts stated. RM1 = large multi-component team award; realistic play is partnering with academic collaborators.

rows.heart: The single capacity-building hub for scaling evidence-based practices across the chronic pain + OUD consortium — one award, $1.75M, and clinician training at the EBP/implementation intersection is its core duty.
rows.eligibility: Forecast lists for-profit organizations as eligible.
rows.notes: FORECAST ONLY (est. due 2026-11-02; NOFO overdue — est. posting 2026-04-20 passed). Funds the network coordination center, NOT the companion implementation trials; single award = competitive.

rows.name: CCBHC Improvement & Advancement (SM-26-015)
rows.program: CCBHC IA for existing clinics; CFDA 93.696; Grants.gov opp 360978
rows.heart: 117 existing CCBHCs are applying for $1M/yr improvement money right now — same 8/17 deadline, same insert-kit: MORE named as the Section C EBP and a Section B workforce-training line.
rows.eligibility: Same statutory limits as SM-26-014 (BH nonprofits, local-gov BH authorities, tribal/Urban Indian orgs) — for-profits excluded; partner play only.
rows.accounts_needed: Partner needs SAM/UEI + Grants.gov + eRA Commons; More Therapy needs none — contractor line in partner budget
rows.scoring_map: A need 10-15 pts (+5 priority pts for high opioid-mortality areas); B implementation 35 pts (staffing/training live here); C EBP 5 pts (name MORE); D experience 25; E data 20
rows.notes: ~117 awards from $117.2M; ≤$1M total costs/yr; up to 4 yrs. accessible models ~$100K training line × 117 applicants (same method as SM-26-014). One campaign covers SM-26-014/-015/-016; the awardee list (≈Nov 2026) then becomes a warm training-customer pipeline.

rows.accounts_needed: None for More Therapy — contracted training/TA vendor inside a state's plan
rows.scoring_map: A need 20; B implementation 35; C experience/staffing 30; D data 15
rows.notes: $12M / 12 awards / 1-yr planning period; winning states' full demonstration applications anticipated due 2028-04-01 — long-game market development. Watch award announcements ~2026-11-15.

rows.name: Alabama ADMH Opioid Settlement Round 4 (RFP 2027-04)
rows.program: Opioid Settlement Grant Program FY2027 (HB487)
rows.heart: Alabama's $8.9M Round 4 requires applicants to articulate evidence-based practices with training, supervision, and fidelity plans — MORE training rides as a subcontract line (capped at 10% of award) in ADMH-certified treatment providers' proposals.
rows.eligibility: Public/private NONPROFITS certified (or certifiable within 4 months) by ADMH — for-profits cannot apply directly; partner path via prior-round awardee lists on the ADMH page.
rows.portal: PAPER ONLY — 1 original + 2 copies + 1 USB physically received by 2:00 pm CT at ADMH Contracts & Purchasing, Montgomery; email/fax not accepted
rows.accounts_needed: Partner needs AL SoS registration, E-Verify, STAARS vendor registration, ADMH certification
rows.match_required: None stated; no supplanting; indirect capped 15%
rows.page_limit: New proposals: cover 1 + org 2 + program 5 + budget 2 pp
rows.scoring_map: 100 pts; program description 30 (EBPs clearly articulated w/ fidelity + training + supervision plans = Section III(e), the MORE slot); understanding 20; experience 15; readiness 15; budget 20
rows.notes: Pools: Treatment $6.251M (≤$350K/award), Prevention $1.786M (≤$75K). accessible = 10% subcontract cap × $350K max treatment award (Q&A Q12), per partner — multiple partner awards possible. 4th annual round; watch mh.alabama.gov each July.

rows.heart: HCAI will fund development and statewide delivery of training modules cross-training MH and SUD providers in substance-use treatment, MAT, and harm reduction for LCSW/LMFT/LPCC/psychologists — a near-exact description of MORE clinician training, with CEU alignment planned.
